world.bio: Sports physiotherapist at a community clinic on Commercial Drive in Vancouver. I treat runners, climbers, and weekend warriors, and I am training for my first Olympic-distance triathlon. I just adopted a rescue puppy named Biscuit who is chewing my entire apartment. Recently I found out my student loan was moved to a different servicer and the interest calculation suddenly looks wrong.
skills_assets: Registered physiotherapist (BC College of Health and Care Professionals), eight years of clinical practice
Specialty in running gait analysis and knee rehab
A spreadsheet tracking her student loan payments since 2019
Triathlon training plan built with a local coach
A small hobby collection of climbing holds at home for finger-strength training
Cypress Mountain season pass (not yet used this year)
Reads academic papers fluently and cross-checks numbers by habit

projects.name: Student loan reconciliation
projects.text: In September I got a letter saying my loan was transferred to a new servicer. The first statement from them shows a balance about $1,400 higher than what I expected from my own spreadsheet, and the interest accrual looks different from the old one. I have been pulling every old statement I can find and building a month-by-month rebuild. It is eating evenings.

projects.name: Olympic-distance triathlon
projects.text: Race is in early next year. Swim twice a week at Hillcrest, bike on the trainer, run along the seawall. Knee is fine; left calf gets tight when mileage jumps.

projects.name: Biscuit the puppy
projects.text: Eleven-week-old rescue, part lab. Chewed a door frame, two shoes, a yoga block. Puppy class starts next week.

notes.text: Biscuit ate the corner of my favorite running shoe overnight. I woke up to a tiny crime scene. I love him but he is a menace.
Clinic day: three ACL post-op patients, one marathoner with ITB pain, one climber with a pulley strain. Left at 7pm, starving. Ate cereal over the sink at 9.

Letter from the loan thing. 'Your account has been transferred.' Fine. Logged in to the new portal. The balance is about $1,400 higher than my spreadsheet says. Either I am wrong or someone is. I hate that I cannot tell which.

Rebuilt payment history through 2022 from bank statements. My numbers keep matching the OLD servicer's last statement, not the new one. So the difference is introduced at the transfer. Wrote it all down.
Long run along the seawall, 18 km. Rain at the end. Feet soaked, spirits high. Thought about the loan mess for the whole first half and then stopped.
Called the new servicer. Forty minutes on hold. The agent said interest capitalized on the transfer date. I asked where that is in my agreement. She said she would send it. Nothing arrived.
Mom asked on the phone if I am saving enough. I said yes. I did not mention the loan. She would worry for a month.
First snow warnings for Cypress. Waxed skis. Thinking about whether to stay in Vancouver for another year or move to Calgary for the Rockies.

messages.text:
Jess: Can you cover Saturday morning?
Me: Yes, but I need Sunday off for a long ride.
Jess: Deal.

Priya: How is the puppy?
Me: He ate my yoga block.
Priya: Send pictures.
Me: [photo]
Priya: He is evil. And adorable.

Tom: Are you still doing the tri?
Me: Yes, 12 weeks of build.
Tom: I'm in for the swim buddy.
Me: Lane 3, 6:30.

Servicer: We have received your inquiry and will respond in 5 to 7 business days.
Me: This is the third time I have asked for the capitalization schedule.
Servicer: Thank you for your patience.

relations.about: Lives in Toronto, supportive, loves dogs.
Runs the local triathlon club, calm and practical.
Retired teacher in Burnaby, worries about money.

constraints: Clinic days are long, so evenings are limited
Cannot afford a lawyer for a loan dispute
Does not want family to worry about money
Swim practice twice a week is non-negotiable
sensitive: The balance gap is about $1,400, which is more than a month of her savings
She feels embarrassed at not understanding interest capitalization
She is considering moving cities and does not know if debt blocks it
